name: Tomás Pablo Korenblit
summary: Finishing a BSc in Data Science focused on Bayesian inference. I build hierarchical Bayesian models of how LLM behavior degrades. My recent work shows that aggregate compliance metrics hide large per-instruction failures, and that stating a preference a model already follows can make it comply less.

bullets: Research on AI Safety. Interests: scalable oversight, interpretability.
Facilitator for BlueDot Impact's Technical AI Safety course
Built a graph database of investors, founders, and companies across the Americas, MENA, and Europe, with warm-intro pathfinding and community detection
Wrote an assistant to turn English into Cypher, so non-technical users can query the graph directly (Python, Neo4j, PostgreSQL, FastAPI, GCP)
Designed a RAG platform to create almost all RLHF annotation interfaces
Wrote validation scripts and dashboards (Python, Looker) used company-wide. Reviewed output quality for the RLHF data teams
Made a lead generation system and trained a classifier for client profiles (Python, Pandas, PostgreSQL, Scikit-learn)

publications.title: PowerBench: Measuring Language Model Bias in Power-shifting Requests
publications.authors: N. Martorell, W. Brau, G. A. Heredia, T. P. Korenblit, G. Labastié, T. Gimenez Molina
bullets: Evaluates 24 models across eight languages and human/AI-agent requesters
Finds nationality biases and greater refusal when AI agents seek power

publications.title: Counterfactual Resampling to Analyse Model Behaviour
publications.venue: BlueDot Impact Technical AI Safety sprint, facilitated by BAISH
bullets: Extends Betley et al.'s Value Leakage introducing per-conversation measurements by resampling truncations of the CoT under a flipped prompt
CoTs that deny being influenced do not concentrate on the influenced traces, against the hypothesis that the model selectively covers its tracks

publications.title: Not All Instructions Are Forgotten Equal
bullets: Measures retention of in-context instructions individually in multi-turn coding sessions
Per-instruction effects range from -2.4 to +5.4 log-odds and only three of twelve instructions benefit from being restated
